name: showreel-c3-lost-day

voice.text: Why did the first sailors around the world lose a whole day? In 1519, five ships left Spain, sailing west. Antonio Pigafetta wrote down every day. Three years later, one ship, the Victoria, was nearly home. In July 1522, they reached Cape Verde. The diary said Wednesday. On shore, it was Thursday. Sailing west, they chased the sun, so each day was a little longer. One lap of the planet cost them one sunrise. Today, the International Date Line puts that day back.

caption:
The first sailors to go around the world came back a day behind the calendar. Here's where that day went. 🌍
